Not closed on candidate sha256:dfedd62f… (source 21e2742e). Severity stays Low and non-mandatory: the shipped engine generates no code, lints clean, and its formula results are unchanged (probe C, exact oracle, 65/65 and 75/75 on Node 22 and 24).

WHAT THE REPAIR (T-DG3-KBE-G, 10472b4) CLOSES. Verified in a disposable clone at 40c84e8, Node 22.
- My round-4 swallow-probe.mjs, run verbatim (sha256 d9989e67…):
  - W1 (catch { }), W2 (finally { return; }) and W4 (Promise….then(…).catch(…)) are now refused by lint AND the scan. In round 4 all three passed every layer.
  - W3, W5 and W6 are refused by lint, the scan and the run-time layer.
- My round-3 guard-layers-probe.mjs, run verbatim: V1 is refused by lint and the scan; V2 by all three layers; S1, S2 and S3 at run time. These match round 4.
- My round-2 guard-bypass-probe.mjs, run verbatim: all 18 forms (O1–O6, N1–N12) are eslint=1 and scan=1.
- The catch selector holds against the shapes I tried:
  - a renamed or destructured parameter, a rethrow after other code, a rethrow in a block or with an else: all refused;
  - shadowing or rebinding EvalError: refused (identifier rule);
  - a later `var e` in the block (S1): it cannot defeat the rethrow, which runs first; refused at run time;
  - an Error[Symbol.hasInstance] hijack that makes `e instanceof EvalError` false (H3 literal key, H4 run-time key): refused at run time, because the hijack is process-wide and breaks the canary's and the injection tests' EvalError assertions. The scan also catches H3; lint does not see Object["defineProperty"] with a string-literal key.
- Event-listener routes (E1 EventTarget, E2 AbortSignal.onabort) are refused at run time: the host reports the listener's EvalError as an unhandled error (7,656 errors, exit 1).
- The other statements check out:
  - the five catch clauses (evaluate.ts, index.ts ×2, parse.ts, value.ts);
  - parse.ts and evaluate.ts change no behaviour;
  - the web (no error boundary or errorElement; React Router 7.9.0's 'Unexpected Application Error!');
  - string-named specifiers;
  - decimal.js (no try/catch/finally/Promise/async/yield);
  - no-unsafe-finally = 2 on all seven closure files.

WHY IT IS NOT CLOSED. My round-4 criterion (a) said that, with the rule enforced statically, 'a self-handled codegen is then refused unless it uses an unexercised path, which is the stated residual'. ADR-0024 §6 now claims exactly that:
- residual, 'Its own handler. It cannot handle its own refusal.';
- layer 3, 'No swallowing. No finally in the closure discards an exception, and the closure has no asynchronous code. So the exception reaches the test on the exercising test's call stack.';
- 'A synchronous engine … This closes a promise reaction that would move the refusal off the exercising test's call stack'.

These statements are not true for new code. On the same exercised path (round-3 S1, tokenize.ts describe(), proved exercised by W5 and G3), two self-handling forms pass ALL THREE layers: lint exit 0, scan exit 0, unit-formula-nocodegen 220 passed + 1 skipped, exit 0, 0 EvalError lines.
- G1: `function* g() { try { codegen } finally { yield 0; } }`, consumed by `g().next()`. The in-flight EvalError is held at the suspended yield and never surfaces.
- G2: the same, then `it.return(0)`. A return completion replaces the pending throw (the 'iterator return()' route).
- A1: asynchrony without any refused spelling. `const p = Array.fromAsync([0]); const { then: t } = p; const d = t.call(p, () => { codegen }); t.call(d, undefined, () => undefined);`. No `Promise` identifier, no `.then` member and no `["then"]`. The rejection is swallowed by the second reaction. A2, the same without the handler, is refused at run time (unhandled rejection), which proves the path runs.

Why no layer sees them:
- Neither lint nor the scan has a rule for generator functions or `yield`.
- no-unsafe-finally covers only return/throw/break/continue, and so does the scan.
- A destructured `then` is neither a MemberExpression nor a `.then`/`["then"]` text match.

In production (no flag), the generated code runs. generator-swallow-demo.log shows the semantics in plain Node 22 and 24: with the flag, nothing reaches the caller; without it, 'generated code ran'.

Minor, same section: 'stricter than no-unsafe-finally' is not quite true. The scan's brace matcher misses `finally { const s = "}"; return; }` (F1), which lint refuses. Layer 1 holds there.

CLOSURE CRITERION (final; I will not ask for further enumeration). Either is enough:
(b) Make §6 exactly true by narrowing the absolute statements:
  - replace 'It cannot handle its own refusal', the 'So the exception reaches the test…' conclusion and the 'This closes a promise reaction…' sentence with an enumerated claim: lint and the scan refuse the listed handler forms (catch shape, finally control flow, Promise/async/.then spellings);
  - state the residual: a self-handling form outside that list, even on an exercised path, is refused by no layer. It is the run-time analogue of Q1–Q5. Examples: generator suspension in a finally (G1/G2), and a promise obtained without the Promise name with a destructured then (A1).
(a) Or ALSO refuse G1/G2/A1 statically, in lint and mirrored in the scan (for example `:function[generator=true]`, `YieldExpression`, a then/catch/finally property key or destructured name, `fromAsync`), and still drop the absolute wording, since another spelling can always exist.
Optionally, correct the 'stricter' sentence (F1).
